newsitem.title: USA: IBM's CEO Gerstner earned $1.5 million in 1996.
newsitem.headline: IBM's CEO Gerstner earned $1.5 million in 1996.

text.p: Louis Gerstner, chairman of International Business Machines Corp., got $1.5 million in salary and $3.3 million in bonuses for 1996, according to the company's proxy statement filed Tuesday.
IBM also granted Gerstner options for 300,000 shares of IBM common stock. The options have a longer vesting period than typical IBM stock options, with no vesting until 1999, the filing said.
It said the award was to encourage Gerstner to stay at IBM for an extended period.

In 1995, Gerstner earned $2 million in salary and $2.8 million as a bonus. In January 1996, his employment agreement was amended to reduce his salary by $500,000 and increase his annual incentive targets by an equivalent amount.
The incentive targets for 1996 were tied to measures of net income and cash flow, creating a direct link between executive pay and company profitability.

The stock option was based on Gerstner's continued contributions to IBM's financial performance, his effective leadership of a fast-changing business and stock option awards to chief executives at other major firms, the company said.
Gerstner earned a payout from the 1994-96 Long-Term Performance Incentive valued at $2,072,567, the filing said. The award was based on IBM financial results over the three-year period.
One half of that was paid in cash and the balance was delivered in stock units that are restricted for two additional years, IBM said in the filing.
At the end of 1996, Gerstner held performance-related stock and other stock and related IBM securities with a combined value of $15.2 million.
Additionally, IBM said FMR Corp., the parent of Fidelity Investments, owned 5.8 percent of IBM as of Feb. 14, according to the proxy statement.
FMR owned a total of 29.8 million shares of IBM.

The filing reported that Edward Johnson, chairman of FMR and Abigail Johnson, director of FMR, together with other family members who are part of a controlling group of FMR, are the beneficial owners of the same shares, except that Edward Johnson's sole voting power is for 34,700 shares.
